credits.s1: How feega credits work: one plan, one-time top-ups, and credits that never expire.
credits.s5: Credits meter AI usage across feega. 100 credits = €1, and credits never expire.
credits.s7: Every AI action spends credits from your workspace balance. The balance is shared by every project in the workspace.
credits.s10: How much a single action spends depends on what it asks for: a short chat reply is a few credits, a long article with its images is many more. The meter follows the work itself, not a fixed price per action: every AI generation and chat turn costs the provider’s price plus 20%.
credits.s40: Monthly credits that you do not spend carry over to the next month. Top-ups stay until spent.

mcp.s14: feega exposes a Model Context Protocol server so coding agents (Cursor, Claude, and others) can read and write a canvas directly — with the same OAuth login as the CLI.
mcp.s16: Authentication is always OAuth (browser login or Bearer from your session).
mcp.s18: Pick a transport: local stdio is simplest on your machine; remote HTTP is for cloud hosts.

mcp.s31: Clients that speak MCP OAuth (opencode, Claude Code, Cursor, the Inspector…) authenticate on their own: on first connect they open feega.app, you approve, and the token is stored by the client. The initial 401 is the start of that handshake, not a crash.
mcp.s32: Custom option — if your client cannot do OAuth, attach the token by hand: Authorization: Bearer <access_token>, using the Supabase access token that feega login saves in ~/.config/feega/session.json. Static API keys (feega_…) are not accepted by the remote server.
